chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a garden containing date palms and trees, some of which had borne fruit and some of which had not. He said: 'There is no objection if it contains what has borne fruit.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who bought a garden containing date palms that contained nothing but green unripe dates. He said: 'No, until they become ready (yazhwu).' I said: 'And what is the readiness (al-zahw)?' He said: 'Until they change color (yatalawwan).'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling a garden with date palms in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *bay' al-thimar* (sale of fruits), distinguishing between mixed orchards where partial fruiting suffices for validity and uniform orchards requiring the fruit to reach *zahw* (the stage of color change and ripening). This ruling ensures the buyer receives a tangible, identifiable asset, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions.
